title: Texts and quick messages
goal: Understand informal text messages and common abbreviations, and write quick messages in the right style for a friend or for your landlord.

items.note: stp = s'il te plaît; svp = s'il vous plaît
mdr = mort de rire (literally “dead from laughing”)
tkt = t'inquiète, short for ne t'inquiète pas
rdv = rendez-vous; also used in notes and calendars
T'es is the spoken form of tu es.

items.en: I'll be there in five minutes.

items.note: In France: À tout à l'heure !

steps.title: A group chat and a text to the landlord
steps.intro: Lucie, Karim and Amira organize a Saturday night out. Later, Amira texts her landlord. Read both screens and compare the style.

blocks.title: Screen 1: The group chat
blocks.fr:
Lucie : Slt tout le monde ! Vous êtes dispo samedi soir ? Resto libanais à 19 h ?
Karim : Oui, super ! C'est où ?
Lucie : Rue Saint-Denis, près du métro. Tkt, j'ai déjà réservé.
Amira : Dsl, je vais arriver un peu en retard. Je finis le travail à 18 h 30.
Lucie : Pas de problème, on t'attend !
Karim : Merci bcp Lucie ! Tu peux mettre l'adresse dans le groupe stp ?
Lucie : Ok, je la mets mtn. Et Karim, prends un taxi cette fois ! Tu t'es perdu la dernière fois, mdr
Karim : Hé ! C'était il y a deux ans ! À samedi !
blocks.en: Lucie: Hi everyone! Are you free Saturday night? Lebanese restaurant at 7 p.m.? / Karim: Yes, great! Where is it? / Lucie: Saint-Denis Street, near the metro. Don't worry, I've already booked. / Amira: Sorry, I'm going to arrive a bit late. I finish work at 6:30. / Lucie: No problem, we'll wait for you! / Karim: Thanks a lot Lucie! Can you put the address in the group please? / Lucie: OK, I'm putting it there now. And Karim, take a taxi this time! You got lost last time, LOL / Karim: Hey! That was two years ago! See you Saturday!

blocks.title: Screen 2: Amira texts her landlord
blocks.fr:
Bonjour Monsieur Gagnon, c'est Amira Benali, de l'appartement 3. Le chauffage ne fonctionne pas depuis ce matin. Est-ce que vous pourriez passer aujourd'hui ? Merci beaucoup.
Amira Benali
blocks.en: Hello Mr. Gagnon, it's Amira Benali from apartment 3. The heating hasn't been working since this morning. Could you come by today? Thank you very much. Amira Benali

blocks.prompt: In the group chat, what does Lucie mean by “Tkt, j'ai déjà réservé”?
blocks.explain: [[tkt]] = [[t'inquiète]] (don't worry). [[J'ai déjà réservé]] = I've already booked (a table).

options: To say sorry because she'll be late
To say she can't come at all
blocks.explain: [[dsl]] = [[désolée]]. She's coming, but [[un peu en retard]] (a bit late) because she finishes work at 18 h 30.

blocks.prompt: Why are there no abbreviations in Amira's text to her landlord?
options: He's not a friend: she uses vous, full words and a polite request
The text is too long for abbreviations
blocks.explain: A text can still be **formal**. With a landlord: [[Bonjour Monsieur…]], [[vous]], full sentences, [[Merci beaucoup]], and your name. Abbreviations are only for friends.

blocks.title: Common abbreviations (recognize them)
head: Abbreviation
Full French
English
rows: s'il te plaît / s'il vous plaît
blocks.note: You don't need to **use** these. You need to **understand** them, because friends, classmates and colleagues will write them to you. When in doubt, write the full word.

blocks.title: Other features of informal writing
blocks.body:
Texts between friends copy the way people **speak**:

- **No ne:** [[Je peux pas venir.]] [[J'ai pas le temps.]]
- **Spoken forms:** [[T'es où ?]] (tu es où ?), [[T'as faim ?]] (tu as faim ?)
- **On instead of nous:** [[On se voit samedi ?]]
- **Short words:** [[dispo]] (disponible), [[resto]] (restaurant), [[appart]] (appartement), [[ordi]] (ordinateur)
- **Questions with intonation only:** [[Tu viens ?]] [[C'est où ?]]
- **Reactions:** [[Ok !]] [[Super !]] [[Trop bien !]] (really great), [[Ouais]] (yeah)

In an email, a form or a message to someone you say vous to, **none** of this belongs.

blocks.title: Same message, two readers
head: To a friend
To your landlord or your boss
rows: Slt ! Dsl, je peux pas venir demain.
Bonjour Madame Roy, je suis désolé, mais je ne peux pas venir demain.
Est-ce que vous êtes disponible jeudi ?
Merci beaucoup. Bonne journée ! + your full name
blocks.note: A polite text is short, but it still has a greeting, full words, vous and your name.

blocks.body:
- [[stp]] with someone you say vous to: write [[s'il vous plaît]] or [[svp]].
- [[tkt]], [[mdr]], [[slt]] in an email to a teacher, a landlord or an employer: far too familiar.
- Writing [[t'es]] or dropping [[ne]] in a formal message: in formal writing, always [[tu es]] and [[ne… pas]].
- Leaving out accents is common in quick texts, but keep them in emails: [[désolé]], [[à]], [[déjà]].
- Don't invent abbreviations. If your reader doesn't understand, the message fails.

- In Québec, people more often write [[lol]] than [[mdr]], which is more typical of France.
- [[À tantôt !]] (see you later today) is everyday Québec French; in France, [[À tout à l'heure !]]
- A text message is [[un texto]] or, in Québec, often [[un texte]] or [[un message texte]]. Your phone is [[un cell]] or [[un cellulaire]] in Québec, [[un portable]] in France.
- You'll also see very informal spellings that copy Québec speech, like [[chu]] for [[je suis]], or [[inquiète-toi pas]] for *don't worry*. Recognize them; don't write them in class or at work.
- [[Bonne fin de semaine !]] is the Québec way to say *have a good weekend*.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat (spoken style)
blocks.note: These are the spoken forms behind the abbreviations. Say them quickly and casually.

lines.tip: T'es sounds like the letter “t” in French: té.

lines.en: I'll be there in five minutes.

lines.tip: In fast speech it sounds like “chais pas”.

blocks.fr: Salut, c'est Karim ! T'inquiète, j'ai pris un taxi. Mais il y a beaucoup de circulation. J'arrive dans dix minutes. Commandez sans moi !
blocks.en: Hi, it's Karim! Don't worry, I took a taxi. But there's a lot of traffic. I'll be there in ten minutes. Order without me!
blocks.prompt: Karim sends a voice message. What does he want his friends to do?
blocks.explain: [[Commandez sans moi !]] = Order without me! He'll be there [[dans dix minutes]].

blocks.fr: Coucou Lucie ! Désolée, je peux pas venir ce soir, ma fille est malade. On se voit la semaine prochaine ? À plus !
blocks.en: Hey Lucie! Sorry, I can't come tonight, my daughter is sick. Shall we see each other next week? See you!
blocks.prompt: Why can't the speaker come tonight?
blocks.explain: [[Ma fille est malade]] = my daughter is sick. Notice the spoken style: [[je peux pas]], without [[ne]].

blocks.prompt: Match each abbreviation with its meaning.
A friend texts: “tkt, c'est pas grave”. What does it mean?
options: Don't worry, it's no big deal
blocks.explain: [[tkt]] = [[t'inquiète]] (don't worry); [[c'est pas grave]] = it's not serious, no problem.

blocks.prompt: You need to tell your landlord the dishwasher is broken. Which text is best?
options: Bonjour Monsieur Gagnon, c'est Raj, appartement 5. Le lave-vaisselle ne marche pas depuis hier. Pourriez-vous passer ? Merci !
Slt ! Le lave-vaisselle marche pas, tu peux passer stp ?
optionFeedback: Slt, tu and stp are for friends.
Too short and too abrupt: no greeting, no name, no thanks.
Coucou and mdr are for close friends, and the problem isn't funny for him.

blocks.prompt: Where are you? (text to a friend)
blocks.explain: Between friends: [[T'es où ?]] or [[Tu es où ?]]. [[Où es-tu ?]] is more careful but correct.

blocks.text: Text: “dsl, je peux pas venir”. In an email to your teacher: “___, je ne peux pas venir.”
blocks.explain: Write the full word, with accents: [[désolé]] (man) or [[désolée]] (woman), and put [[ne]] back: [[je ne peux pas]].

blocks.prompt: I'll be there in five minutes.
blocks.explain: French uses the present [[j'arrive]] for *I'll be there*, and [[dans]] for *in* (time from now).

blocks.text: Karim, tu t'es ___ la dernière fois !
blocks.en: Karim, you got lost last time!
blocks.explain: [[Se perdre]] is reflexive, so it takes être in the passé composé: [[tu t'es perdu]].

blocks.prompt: Don't worry, I've already booked. (to a friend)
accept: Ne t'inquiète pas, j'ai déjà réservé.
Ne t'inquiète pas, j'ai déjà fait la réservation.
blocks.explain: [[Ne t'inquiète pas]] is the full form; friends say [[t'inquiète]] and write [[tkt]]. [[Déjà]] goes between the auxiliary and the participle.

blocks.fr: Désolée, je vais arriver un peu en retard.
accept: Désolé, je vais arriver un peu en retard.
blocks.explain: Futur proche: [[je vais arriver]]. [[En retard]] = late.

blocks.prompt: Write two quick messages (40–70 words in total). 1) Reply to Lucie's group chat: accept, say you'll be late and why, and ask one question; you can use two or three abbreviations. 2) Text your neighbour, Madame Lavoie, whom you don't know well: your package was delivered to her door by mistake, and you ask when you can pick it up. No abbreviations.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez deux messages rapides : un à vos amis, un à votre voisine.
checklist: Message 1: tu / on, informal greeting, 2–3 abbreviations you understand
Message 1: a reason for being late and a question
Message 2: Bonjour Madame Lavoie, + who you are (apartment number)
Message 2: vous, full words, a polite question with est-ce que or pourriez-vous

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
Slt Lucie ! Oui, je viens ! Mais dsl, je vais arriver vers 19 h 30, j'ai un cours de français. C'est quel resto ? Merci bcp !

Bonjour Madame Lavoie, c'est Mei, de l'appartement 4. Le livreur a laissé mon colis devant votre porte. Quand est-ce que je peux passer le chercher ? Merci beaucoup ! Mei Chen
models.en: Hi Lucie! Yes, I'm coming! But sorry, I'll arrive around 7:30, I have a French class. Which restaurant is it? Thanks a lot! / Hello Ms. Lavoie, it's Mei from apartment 4. The delivery person left my package in front of your door. When can I come and get it? Thank you very much! Mei Chen

models.label: Stronger model answer
models.fr:
Cc tout le monde ! Super idée ! Je viens, mais je vais être un peu en retard : je travaille jusqu'à 19 h. Commandez sans moi, tkt ! On partage l'addition ?

Bonjour Madame Lavoie, c'est Olivier Martin, de l'appartement 2. Je pense que le livreur a laissé un colis pour moi chez vous ce matin. Est-ce que je pourrais passer le chercher ce soir, vers 18 h ? Merci d'avance et bonne journée ! Olivier
models.en: Hey everyone! Great idea! I'm coming, but I'll be a bit late: I work until 7. Order without me, don't worry! Shall we split the bill? / Hello Ms. Lavoie, it's Olivier Martin from apartment 2. I think the delivery person left a package for me at your place this morning. Could I come and get it tonight, around 6 p.m.? Thanks in advance and have a good day! Olivier

blocks.prompt: Send a voice message to a friend (20 seconds): you're on your way to the restaurant, you'll be late, say why and when you'll arrive, and tell them what to do.
blocks.promptFr: Envoyez un message vocal à un ami.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut, c'est Raj ! Désolé, le métro est en panne. J'arrive dans vingt minutes. Commandez sans moi, je vais prendre la même chose que Karim. À tantôt !
models.en: Hi, it's Raj! Sorry, the metro has broken down. I'll be there in twenty minutes. Order without me, I'll have the same thing as Karim. See you soon!

summary:
- Recognize common texting abbreviations: [[slt, bcp, stp, dsl, tkt, mdr, jsp, rdv]]
- Understand informal style: no [[ne]], [[t'es]], [[on]], short words like [[dispo]] and [[resto]]
- Write a quick text to a friend, and a short, polite text with vous and full words to a landlord or neighbour

meta.author: ai
meta.notes: Replaced the reorder distractor en (J'arrive en cinq minutes is also grammatical) with à. Gave Raj a different apartment number than Amira, added Je suis désolé(e) to r5, added article/gender to rdv, and made the formal table example more natural.
